guard: attach redeems a session grant with the seed the MESH resolved, never one walked up from the cwd, and a cwd anchor holding another chain for the same space is reported rather than obeyed
command: pnpm --filter @cotal-ai/workspace build && pnpm --filter @cotal-ai/cli build && pnpm smoke:attach-auth-root
why: EVERY ATTACH CELL RUNS THE BINARY, so the command builds first. The suite drives `tsx
bin/cotal.ts` and `@cotal-ai/cli` resolves to `dist/`, so a mutation on `src` that is not built
is a mutation the run never sees: it would come back SURVIVED and read as `this line does not
matter` when what was measured is `this line was not in the artifact`. `@cotal-ai/workspace`
builds first because the CLI's dist consumes it, and mutations 3 and 4 live there.
MUTATION 1 IS THE DEFECT ITSELF, restored verbatim rather than approximated: the pre-fix line
asked the CURRENT DIRECTORY which root holds the seed, after resolution had already answered
that question and connected with its answer. It is written with local aliases only because the
fix deleted those three imports from the file; the expression is the one that shipped.
WHAT MUTATION 1 PROVES AND WHAT IT DOES NOT. It proves the fossil cell REACHES the redemption
seed and depends on which chain it comes from -- the credential is minted from the cwd's dead
chain and the broker rejects it. It does not prove the cell would catch a defect anywhere else
on the attach path, and nothing here claims that.
MUTATION 2 IS THE OTHER HALF OF THE FIX AND IS NOT REDUNDANT WITH 1. Carrying the resolution's
seed forward makes attach CORRECT; reporting the divergent anchor makes it LEGIBLE. Delete the
report and every functional cell in this suite still passes, which is exactly the state issue
#722 was found in: the command worked or failed for a reason the operator had no way to see.
MUTATIONS 3 AND 4 ARE THE DETECTOR'S TWO FALSE DIRECTIONS, one each. 3 makes it blind whenever
the resolved root also holds a chain (a false NEGATIVE: the divergent anchor stops being
reported). 4 makes it fire from any directory that merely lacks auth (a false POSITIVE: every
unanchored directory grows a warning about a trust chain that does not exist). A detector is
only worth its output if BOTH directions are held, and a suite that pinned one and not the
other would let the other regress silently.
NOT GRADED, and said rather than implied: the arm of the no-seed refusal for a connection with
no resolved root. No supported route reaches redemption in that state -- both off-registry
routes are refused earlier, which the suite MEASURES in cells D -- so there is no mutation for
it here. An unreachable arm cannot be killed, and a mutation aimed at one would report
SURVIVED and read as a coverage gap rather than as the invariant it actually is.
MUTATIONS 5 AND 6 ARE THE SECOND ANSWER IN ITS OTHER FORM. Carrying the resolution's seed forward
stops the cwd choosing WHICH chain is used; it does not stop the cwd ending the command. The
detector reads the walked root before the mint, and `loadSpaceAuth` refuses unreadable trust
material loudly, so a corrupt `broker.json` up the walk aborted an attach that had already
declared it was not using that root -- and on the reconnect path that abort is classified
transient and retried forever. 5 restores that shape whole and is graded through the binary. 6 is
the half fix, guarding only the side the bug report named, and it is not redundant: an unreadable
RESOLVED root leaves nothing to compare against, and reporting a divergence from it would be a
claim this code cannot support.
THE ONE INPUT THAT IS NOT GRADED, and said rather than implied: a process whose working directory
has been DELETED. `findCotalRoot` defaults its argument to `process.cwd()`, which throws on that
input, which is why the call sits inside the guard rather than before it. There is no mutation and
no cell for it because the only way to produce it is to chdir into a directory and remove it, and
this suite process goes on to read fixtures and spawn the real binary afterwards: a cell that
sabotages its own process's cwd would take the other twenty four with it. An explicit path cannot
stand in, since a non-existent PATH walks to the filesystem root and returns normally. The guard is
structural instead, and the contract comment states the bound.

mutations.name: the defect restored: redemption walks up from the cwd for the seed instead of using the one the mesh resolved
mutations.replace:
const { authDir: mAuthDir, findCotalRoot: mFind, loadSpaceAuth: mLoad } = await import("@cotal-ai/workspace");
  const auth = mLoad(mAuthDir(mFind()), t.space);
mutations.expectRed: attach from a fossil-anchored directory redeems and opens the session
mutations.cell: attach from a fossil-anchored directory redeems and opens the session
mutations.note: This is issue #722 verbatim. The cwd holds a fossil `.cotal` whose chain the broker does not trust, so the session-caller credential is minted from it and the connect is refused.

mutations.name: the divergent-anchor report is deleted, leaving the command correct and the operator blind
mutations.expectRed: …and the shadowing anchor is REPORTED, naming the walked root and the one actually used
mutations.cell: …and the shadowing anchor is REPORTED, naming the walked root and the one actually used
mutations.note: A careless edit, not a malicious one: the report is dropped and the detector call kept. Everything still typechecks and every functional cell still passes.

mutations.name: the detector goes blind whenever the resolved root also holds a chain (false negative)
mutations.expectRed: a cwd anchor carrying a DIFFERENT chain for the space is detected, and names that root
mutations.cell: a cwd anchor carrying a DIFFERENT chain for the space is detected, and names that root
mutations.note: The resolved root holds a chain in every real mesh, so this silences the detector everywhere it matters while leaving it green on the cells where nothing should be reported.

mutations.name: the detector fires from any directory that merely lacks auth (false positive)
mutations.expectRed: standing where there is no anchor at all says nothing
mutations.cell: standing where there is no anchor at all says nothing
mutations.note: Turns the report into noise: every directory outside a checkout would warn about a trust chain it does not have, which is how a real signal gets trained away.

mutations.name: the detector can throw again: an unreadable root on the way past aborts a command that is not using it
mutations.expectRed: attach from a directory whose ancestor auth is CORRUPT still opens the session
mutations.cell: attach from a directory whose ancestor auth is CORRUPT still opens the session
mutations.note: The shape the first fix shipped in. `loadSpaceAuth` throws on trust material it cannot read, so a half-written `broker.json` anywhere up the cwd walk kills an attach whose seed came from the resolved root. Graded through the REAL binary, because that is where the abort is fatal.

mutations.name: only the walked root is guarded, so an unreadable RESOLVED root still throws (the half fix)
mutations.expectRed: …and so does an unreadable RESOLVED root, rather than claiming a divergence it cannot see
mutations.cell: …and so does an unreadable RESOLVED root, rather than claiming a divergence it cannot see
mutations.note: The fix someone writes after reading only the bug report: guard the side the report named. The other side is the same abort with the roots swapped, and it is the direction a later change is most likely to reintroduce.

mutations.name: CONTROL the attach seed-output assertion is live in its suite file
mutations.find: ![fromFossil, fromBare, fromCorrupt].some((o) => /(?:^|\n)(?:✓ added @cotal-ai\/|→ wrote operator-global seed store payload)/.test(o)),
mutations.expectRed: the attached-session subprocess does not reconcile connector payloads before exercising attach
mutations.cell: the attached-session subprocess does not reconcile connector payloads before exercising attach
mutations.note: Positive control for the same-file reach requirement. It proves the suite executes the seed-output assertion before the seed-skip mutation is graded.

mutations.name: the attached-session subprocess loses the seed-skip guard and reconciles before attach
mutations.find:
cwd,
    env: { ...cleanEnv, COTAL_HOME: home, XDG_CONFIG_HOME: join(home, "xdg"), COTAL_SKIP_CONNECTOR_SEED: "1", NO_COLOR: "1" },
    stdio:
mutations.replace:
cwd,
    env: { ...cleanEnv, COTAL_HOME: home, XDG_CONFIG_HOME: join(home, "xdg"), NO_COLOR: "1" },
    stdio:
mutations.expectRed: the attached-session subprocess does not reconcile connector payloads before exercising attach
mutations.cell: the attached-session subprocess does not reconcile connector payloads before exercising attach
mutations.note: The attach subprocess must reach the attach path directly. Without the skip, the command auto-reconciles connector payloads first; its seed output can consume the bounded window and hide both the attached banner and the divergent-root report.
